comments.body:
Fresh v2 datapoints from the 2026-07-22 follow-up:

- The v2 compiler currently exposes 432 project units and 334 distinct generated headers from `compiler/v2/src`.
- 333 units are scoped, but 99 still require broad fallback publication because their body-level dependency evidence is not yet expressible precisely enough.
- `compile/pipeline/fixture_runner.phs` is the clearest example: it is a real coordinator that touches frontend reuse, symbol/fact extraction, references/contracts, capability/readiness, storage/lifetime, backend lowering, LLVM text emission, object output, and link/coordinator proof paths. Under today’s project-unit model, that kind of coordinator becomes a broad invalidation source.
- `compile/support/proof_metrics.phs` shows the complementary problem: central proof-counter catalogs become high-fanout even when a change is conceptually local to one stage or one measurement proof.

Why this matters for modules: v2 would benefit from first-class compile-time surfaces where a module publishes stable public rows/contracts separately from private implementation and proof plumbing. The module interface hash could stay unchanged while internals move around, and coordinator modules could depend on named surfaces instead of causing wide generated-header publication. This also lines up with the Simple C++ metaprogramming direction: project-visible compile-time surfaces need stable version/shape identity, not just textual inclusion.

Follow-up from the v2 local mitigation batch (`simple-cpp-compiler` commit `4840c64f`): v2 added a small `compile/support/mt_publication_metrics.phs` helper so downstream MT publication counters can evolve without changing the central proof metric catalog first.

That local shape is useful but manual. The build data shows why first-class modules/surfaces would help:

- The project now has 433 source units and 335 distinct generated project-unit headers.
- The new helper is conceptually a small private implementation surface, but the first validation still rebuilt 433 generated objects.
- `fixture_runner.phs` remains a broad coordinator with real dependencies across many stages; it is the kind of file that should depend on named public surfaces rather than textual generated-header reach.
- Warm no-change is clean immediately after, so the pain is invalidation/publication breadth after edits, not Ninja failing to detect no-work.

A Simple C++ module system with explicit public compile-time surfaces, private implementation hashes, and cached module artifacts would let v2 express this intent directly instead of manually carving helper files while still paying broad generated recompilation.

Update from branch `codex/compiler-vector-runtime` pushed to origin at `c0a498db`.

Issue #221 work completed on this branch:

- `c29ada70` Resolve #221 project module surface reporting
- `18437a08` Validate project module dependencies
- `a313f233` Add project module dependency summary cache
- `e9c0de76` Add module-based generated build grouping
- `5493034b` Validate project module public APIs
- `36c5e25a` Add build planner warm state

Implemented:

- explicit `project_modules` config surface with named project-local modules
- module public surface and private implementation artifacts under `.prism/cache/project_modules/`
- `scpp explain-build modules` and `scpp explain-build module <name>` views
- generated object compile inputs wired to owning/dependency public module surface artifacts, with private implementation artifacts excluded from consumer compile inputs
- `project_module_dependency_policy` with report/warn/fail behavior against source dependency evidence
- per-module dependency summary artifacts and cache hit/new/changed/unavailable reporting
- release-mode module grouping via `build.grouping_policy = "module"` plus `build.grouping_compile = true`
- `project_module_public_policy` with declaration-target validation for non-empty `public_exports`
- planner warm-state snapshot now records module summary hashes

Clarification: modules are explicit. Simple C++ does not auto-propose module boundaries.

Validation run across the branch included:

- `php tests/tools/test_scpp_project_module_dependency_validation.php`
- `php tests/tools/test_scpp_project_module_public_api_validation.php`
- `php tests/tools/test_scpp_project_module_stan_summary_cache.php`
- `php tests/tools/test_scpp_build_grouping_module.php`
- `php tests/tools/test_scpp_explain_build.php`
- `php tests/tools/test_scpp_build_planner_state.php`
- sandbox compiler no-op build from `sandbox/issue_215/compiler_v2_src`: 388 skipped, Ninja no work

Known remaining debt is tracked in `specs/planning/issues_219_220_221_build_debt_backlog_2026_07_22.md`: modules are project-local, transitive boundary enforcement and method/property-level module API modeling are not implemented, native/dependency/singleton module units remain per-source, and module cache data does not yet skip STAN semantic work.

title: Compiler modules: project-level compile-time surfaces and cached module artifacts
